newsitem.title: USA: Key tobacco negotiator has White House meeting.
newsitem.headline: Key tobacco negotiator has White House meeting.

text.p: A key negotiator in talks aimed at settling lawsuits against cigarette makers, Mississippi state attorney general Mike Moore, gave the White House an update on the negotiations on Wednesday.
White House spokesman Barry Toiv said the deputy White House legal counsel, Bruce Lindsey, met with Moore and planned to talk to other parties in the talks during the day.
Toiv described the meeting as part of the White House's ongoing effort to monitor the tobacco negotiations.

A total of 32 states are suing cigarette makers to recover Medicaid money spent on treating smoking-related illnesses. The industry wants protection from legal damages but the attorneys general are reluctant to give tobacco companies the immunity from lawsuits they seek.
Mississippi's case is scheduled to be the first to go to trial, on July 7. Moore hoped to know by next week whether a deal could be reached or if he should get ready for trial.

The White House said on Monday a tobacco settlement proposal seemed to be a long way off. Spokesman Mike McCurry said any deal "is going to require a very careful review" with an eye toward ensuring "the best possible public health outcome."
